evidence.kb:reentrancy:name: Reentrancy
evidence.kb:reentrancy:description: An external call can let another contract re-enter before the caller has finished updating its state.
evidence.kb:reentrancy:root_cause: An invariant is temporarily broken across an external call.
evidence.kb:reentrancy:mitigation: Update state before external calls and consider a reentrancy guard; examine cross-function paths too.
evidence.kb:reentrancy:fact:mechanism: A contract interaction transfers control to the called contract, which may call back.
evidence.kb:reentrancy:fact:scope: Reentrancy is not limited to Ether transfers; calls to other contracts can also create re-entry paths.
evidence.kb:reentrancy:fact:pattern: The checks-effects-interactions pattern performs checks, then state changes, then external interactions.

posts.text: Reentrancy can let a contract be called again before it finishes updating its state.
When a contract calls another, control passes to the callee, which may call back.
The risk is not limited to Ether transfers; any call to another contract can create a re-entry path.
Update state before external calls and consider a reentrancy guard. Follow the checks-effects-interactions pattern: checks, then state changes, then external interactions.
Given that an invariant is temporarily broken during an external call, have you verified that no re-entry paths remain?

evidence.kb:unchecked-return:name: Unchecked external call result
evidence.kb:unchecked-return:description: Ignoring a failed low-level call can leave the contract proceeding as if an operation succeeded.
evidence.kb:unchecked-return:root_cause: The caller does not check the success flag returned by a low-level call.
evidence.kb:unchecked-return:mitigation: Check call outcomes and define explicit failure handling.
evidence.kb:unchecked-return:fact:mechanism: Low-level calls expose a success flag that the caller can inspect.
evidence.kb:unchecked-return:fact:consequence: If failure is ignored, subsequent logic may rely on an operation that did not complete.
evidence.kb:unchecked-return:fact:review: The failure path needs explicit handling, not only a check of the successful path.

posts.text: Unchecked external call result appears when a low-level call fails and its return value is ignored. The contract then proceeds as if the operation succeeded.
Low-level calls expose a success flag that the caller can inspect.
The root cause is that the caller does not check the success flag returned by the low-level call.
If the failure is ignored, later logic may rely on an operation that never completed.
Mitigate by checking call outcomes and defining explicit failure handling. Ensure the failure path is handled, not just the success branch. How do you verify external call results?

evidence.kb:access-control:name: Missing access control
evidence.kb:access-control:description: A sensitive function without adequate authorization can be called by an unintended account.
evidence.kb:access-control:root_cause: Permissions are missing or applied inconsistently across privileged entry points.
evidence.kb:access-control:mitigation: Define roles explicitly and test unauthorized calls for every privileged operation.
evidence.kb:access-control:fact:scope: Different privileged operations can require different roles.
evidence.kb:access-control:fact:lifecycle: Role assignment and removal are themselves permission-sensitive operations.
evidence.kb:access-control:fact:review: Access control design includes deciding who may grant and revoke permissions.

posts.text: A privileged function that lacks proper authorization can be invoked by an unintended account.
The root cause is missing or inconsistently applied permission checks across privileged entry points.
Various privileged operations may need distinct roles, so a single missing check can affect multiple functions.
Mitigate by defining explicit roles and testing unauthorized calls for each privileged operation.
How do you plan to confirm that role assignment and revocation themselves require proper permission and that only authorized accounts can grant or remove roles?
